item.title: Levenberg-Marquardt Method
item.description: The Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) method damps each Gauss–Newton step: \big(J^\top J+\lambda\,L_{\text{LM}}\big)\,\delta = -J^\top r , with a damping parameter \lambda>0 and a symmetric positive definite matrix L_{\text{LM}}.

item.title: Bayesian Inversion
item.description: In the Bayesian (statistical) approach, the unknown conductivity \sigma and the data y are random variables.

item.title: Parametrizations of the Conductivity
item.description: The unknowns of a reconstruction need not be the coefficients of the conductivity in the finite element space of the forward model.

item.title: Resolution and Confidence Maps
item.description: A reconstruction does not determine every part of the conductivity equally well.

item.title: Regularization
item.description: Classical regularisation of the ill-posed EIT problem: penalties that encode prior knowledge, and how to weigh them against the data. Reading order.

item.title: ModularEIT Wiki
item.description: A wiki on the theory of Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT): imaging the electrical conductivity inside a body from currents and voltages measured at its surface.

item.title: Anatomy of an EIT Reconstruction
item.description: An iterative EIT reconstruction repeatedly compares simulated with measured data and improves the conductivity. It combines five exchangeable pieces.

item.title: Choosing a Linear Solver
item.description: The systems A(\sigma)X = B of EIT are sparse, symmetric and positive semidefinite.

item.title: Choosing an Optimizer
item.description: Which method minimises J(\sigma) = \Phi(\sigma)+\alpha R(\sigma) best depends mainly on two properties: whether the misfit \Phi is a sum of squares, and whether the regulariser R is smooth.
